adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106 — dateOverrides passed into checkIfIsAvailable are never filtered by userId, so one user's date override (block/open) can incorrectly gate another user's slot availability when checking team/collective schedules

adjudication.rationale: In getSchedule, `dateOverrides` is built by `userAvailability.flatMap(...)` and includes overrides for all users (now with `userId` and `timeZone`). But `checkIfIsAvailable` accepts `dateOverrides?: { start: Date; end: Date; }[]` (no `userId`) and iterates `dateOverrides.find(...)` over the entire array without filtering by the slot’s user/host. Calls to `checkIfIsAvailable` spread `...availabilityCheckProps` (which includes the aggregated `dateOverrides`) for availability checks across different users’ schedules, so one user’s override can cause `return false`/`return true` for another user’s slot on the same day. The diff shows no per-user filtering before passing `dateOverrides` into `checkIfIsAvailable`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:211 — override.timeZone` may be undefined for overrides whose availability schedule has no explicit timeZone, so `dayjs(...).tz(undefined)` silently falls back to an implicit/local zone rather than the organizer's actual zone, producing a wrong offset without any error propagation

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new logic computes offsets via `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`, but `override.timeZone` is not guaranteed to exist: the diff explicitly makes `TimeRange.timeZone?: string` optional (`packages/types/schedule.d.ts`), and `getSchedule` populates `timeZone: availability.timeZone` without any fallback if `availability.timeZone` is missing. There is no guard/default in `getSlots` for `override.timeZone`, so an undefined zone can flow into `.tz(...)`, which can lead to an implicit/default timezone being used (or otherwise incorrect offset computation), producing wrong slot boundaries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — Even if the equality bug above were fixed, using `===`/`.isSame()` on the exact millisecond-adjusted start vs end time as a "full day blocked" sentinel is fragile compared to checking `override.start` and `override.end` on the raw override object (pre-offset) since floating point/DST edge cases in the offset add could make legitimately-equal times fail to compare equal

adjudication.rationale: The cited logic in `checkIfIsAvailable` does not use `.isSame()` for the “full day blocked” sentinel; it uses strict `===` between two Dayjs objects (`dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)`), which is a different (and in fact always-false) issue. The finding’s claim about fragility due to millisecond/DST/floating-point effects in an `.isSame()` comparison on offset-adjusted times is not directly supported by the diff as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:103 — checkIfIsAvailable's dateOverrides.find() iterates the globally-flattened dateOverrides list without filtering by userId, so one host's date override in a collective/round-robin event can incorrectly block or approve another host's slots

adjudication.rationale: In getSchedule, `dateOverrides` is flattened across all `userAvailability` entries into one array with `userId` (and now `timeZone`) but is passed wholesale via `availabilityCheckProps` into `checkIfIsAvailable` for slot checks across different users. Inside `checkIfIsAvailable` (around the added `dateOverrides.find(...)` block), the logic never filters by `userId`/slot user, so any override matching the slot’s day can set `dateOverrideExist` and cause the function to return `true`/`false` for a slot even when that override belongs to a different host. This can incorrectly approve/block slots in multi-host scenarios (collective/round-robin).
